plugins.name: strategy-consultant
plugins.description: Performs the analytical work of a strategy consultant — from problem definition through research, sense-checking, synthesis, and executive-grade client deliverables. Deploys independent research agents and validates findings for accuracy before producing a clear, cliché-free written report.

skills.name: client-report
skills.description: Package synthesized findings into an executive-grade Word document (.docx) deliverable. Use when someone asks to "write the report", "create the deliverable", "produce the client document", "draft the final report", "package this into a document", or when the analytical workflow reaches the final delivery phase after synthesis. Also trigger when someone has a completed storyline and needs it turned into a professional, client-ready written report.
headings: Preflight Gate (run BEFORE any other step)
Research Notes (mandatory — always the final section)
Step 2: Draft the Executive Summary First

skills.name: engagement-manager
skills.description: Run a full strategy consulting analytical engagement from problem definition through to a client-ready report. Use when someone asks to "run a full analysis", "do a consulting engagement on", "analyze this end to end", "help me with a client engagement", "do the full workflow", or presents a business problem that needs the complete Define → Research → Sense-Check → Synthesize → Deliver treatment. This is the orchestrator skill — it coordinates all other skills in the plugin to produce a comprehensive deliverable.
headings: Strategy Consulting Engagement — Full Analytical Workflow
Shared references (read once; linked from every phase)
Skill invocation rule (applies to every phase below)
Resume behavior (mandatory at the start of every `/engagement` invocation)
Phase 2.5: Data Source Inquiry (MANDATORY — three required questions)
Phase 3.5: Expert Interviews (if indicated in Phase 2.5)
Phase 4: Sense-Check (MANDATORY — produces a written report)
Phase 5: Synthesize (MANDATORY — produces a written storyline)
Phase 5.5: Storyline Critique (MANDATORY — independent critic, not the synthesizer)

skills.name: expert-interview
skills.description: Internal phase of the strategy-consultant engagement — invoke via engagement-manager, not directly. Plan, guide, and process expert interviews to confirm and enhance research findings. Use when someone asks to "prepare for expert interviews", "create an interview guide", "who should we interview", "process interview notes", "extract insights from interviews", or when the analytical workflow includes expert interviews after the research phase. Also trigger when someone uploads expert interview transcripts or notes that need to be analyzed and integrated into the research base.
headings: Expert Interview — Confirm, Enhance, and Challenge Research Findings
Preflight Gate (run BEFORE any other step)
Phase 1: Interview Planning — Who to Interview
Step 1: Identify Information Gaps That Experts Can Close
Step 1: Review Research Findings Relevant to This Expert
Phase 3: Information Extraction — Processing Interview Notes
Step 4: Produce the Expert Interview Output

skills.name: hypothesis-tree
skills.description: Build a structured hypothesis tree with testable branches to guide analysis. Use when someone asks to "build a hypothesis tree", "structure this problem into hypotheses", "create an issue tree", "break this down MECE", or when a defined problem would benefit from structured decomposition before research begins. This skill is optional — not every problem requires a formal hypothesis tree. Skip it when the question is narrow enough that direct research is more efficient.
headings: Step 1: Start with the Governing Hypothesis
Step 3: Define What Proves or Disproves Each Branch

skills.name: problem-definition
skills.description: Internal phase of the strategy-consultant engagement — invoke via engagement-manager, not directly. Define and scope a client problem into a sharp, decision-oriented question. Use when someone says "help me define this problem", "scope this engagement", "what's the real question here", "sharpen this problem statement", or provides a vague business challenge that needs structuring before analysis can begin. Also trigger when someone shares a client brief, RFP, or project description and needs help extracting the core analytical question.
headings: Routing Check (run BEFORE any other step)
What a Good Problem Statement Contains
Step 4.5: Envision the Best Possible Answer (MANDATORY)
Step 6: Extract the Client Question Checklist

skills.name: research
skills.description: Internal phase of the strategy-consultant engagement — invoke via engagement-manager, not directly. Conduct thorough, multi-tier research on a client question by dispatching two independent research agents and a validation agent. Use when someone asks to "research this topic", "find evidence for", "investigate this market", "gather data on", "what does the evidence say about", or when the analytical workflow reaches the research phase after problem definition. Also trigger when someone uploads client data or expert interview notes that need to be analyzed alongside public research.
headings: Preflight Gate (run BEFORE any other step)
Data Source Priority Hierarchy and Scenarios
Step 0: Data Source Inquiry (deferred to engagement-manager Phase 2.5)
Step 2: Generate Differentiated Research Angles (DYNAMIC — do not use fixed categories)
Step 3: Dispatch Agents in Parallel (BOTH agents required)
Step 5.5: Answer Altitude Check (MANDATORY — before compiling the research package)

skills.name: sense-check
skills.description: Pressure-test research findings and analytical conclusions for robustness. Use when someone asks to "sense-check this", "pressure-test these findings", "challenge this analysis", "stress-test the argument", "play devil's advocate", "poke holes in this", or when the analytical workflow needs a quality gate between research and synthesis. Also trigger when someone presents a conclusion and wants it challenged before taking it to a client.
headings: Preflight Gate (run BEFORE any other step)
Step 3: Steel-Man the Opposite AND Surface Client-Raised Objections
Coverage Matrix (if Deliverable Blueprint has Coverage Dimensions)

skills.name: synthesis
skills.description: Synthesize research findings into a coherent storyline that answers the client question. Use when someone asks to "synthesize these findings", "build the storyline", "what's the narrative", "put this together into a story", "structure the argument", "what should we tell the client", or when the analytical workflow moves from sense-checked research to constructing the client-facing argument. Also trigger when someone has a collection of findings and needs help turning them into a logical, persuasive narrative.
headings: Preflight Gate (run BEFORE any other step)
Core Principle: Let the Answer Shape the Structure
Step 0: Precision Anchor Re-Check (mandatory before writing anything)
Step 3: Stack the Evidence Under Each Argument
Step 4: Address the Counter-Arguments (comprehensive, not single-risk)

headings: CONTINUATION COMMAND — do not use as a fresh entry point
